comments: Child denies the assignment of an object in response to MOT's question 'für wen is(t) das?'
Target 'alle' in 'alle raus' is used as a quantifier ('all/everything out'), not as a negation meaning 'all gone'.
Child rejects mother's interpretation of the proposed action (driving the stroller) in line 4950.
Child says 'nein da' (no there), vetoing the current placement of an object and proposing a new one.
Child rejects the mother's proposed manner of lying down ('noch mal so?'), proposing a different way.
Child opposes the action of fetching the stool, agreeing with the mother's assessment that it is not needed and explaining they fit well where they are.
Child is playing a 'here/gone' game with the beetle; 'weg' asserts the beetle's absence from view.
Child corrects the identity of the person they want to show the car to, responding to the adult's correction in line 125899.
Child opposes Thorsten's claim to get the Flipper by asserting he already has a toy; this functions as a rejection of the proposed action.
Child refuses the grandfather's prompts to take or do something (e.g., 'nimm doch', 'komm mal hier').
Child denies that the object is for the father ('is der für n Papi?') and asserts it is their own money ('mein deld').
Child denies the proposition that 'we' are getting the money, correcting the fact to 'Mama' in the following turn.
Child resists the proposed action of moving over (line 217357).
Child responds 'nein' to mother's question about whether they want to paint anymore (line 240927), effectively rejecting further painting.
Child denies mother's claim that she has soiled her pants (line 250007).
Child reports that items do not fit, echoing father's observation (line 272626) and confirmed by father's 'too small' (line 272630).
Child reports that something does not fit into the car ('geht nicht rein'), which is a report of a failed attempt/non-holding property.
Child refuses to put on shoes, confirmed by mother's 'doch' (line 280332) and subsequent discussion of shoe fit.
Child answers Mother's question 'is(t) da ein Spiegel?' by stating the mirror is absent.
Child reports the factual state that the toy phone does not turn on/work, following the statement that it is broken.
Child reacts to adult's 'schon fertig' (already finished) by questioning if there is no more left.
Child states the lid is gone/missing, confirming the mother's statement in line 281766.
Child contradicts mother's claim in line 282477 that the animal is just born.
Child opposes the dog having a ball in its mouth after MOT's observation in line 282611.
Child makes a factual statement that the mouse cannot eat the snail.
Child states they do not know the name of the animal in response to mother's prompt (line 282764).
The token 'alle' is used as a quantifier meaning 'all of them' (confirmed by adult's 'du willst alles haben?'), not as a negation meaning 'all gone'.
Child reports a failed attempt or property ('it doesn't work/fit') during play; similar to Example T.
Child reports that an object does not fit into a slot; this is a factual report of a failed attempt, matching Example T.
Child says 'will das nicht' (don't want that) while struggling with a toy, functioning as a rejection of the item/activity.
Child denies mother's question about whether they want to play more (line 283525).
Child expresses refusal of an item ("will das nisch").
Child refuses to continue the activity of building after mother's warnings about breaking toys.
Child answers mother's question 'what do you want to do?' by stating they want to do nothing, indicating the absence of a desired activity.
Child refuses the mother's directive to tidy up ('einräum(e)n'), confirmed by subsequent 'ich will noch weiter machen'.
Child reports that something (likely the train set) does not work/fit; matches Example T.
Child reports that an object does not fit or work while tidying up; matches Example T.
Child is playing phone; 'nee' is followed by 'hier sind keiner da', indicating the absence of the other person.
Child remarks that there is nothing inside the container, following mother's comment "alles leer".
Child refuses the mother's request to tidy up ('räums(t) du bitte mal auf?').
Child vetoes a proposed placement implied by mother's 'guck' and proposes an alternative ('da dran').
Child denies the caregiver's claim that she is a sheep (line 360230), clarifying her identity as Anna Luca.
